text.tspan: Extreme monetary poverty and multidimensional poverty over time
Multidimensional poverty is defined as being deprived in a range of health, education and living standards
indicators. Extreme poverty is defined as living below the International Poverty Line of $3 per day.
Data source: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform (2026); Alkire et al. (2025) - The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2025
Note: Extreme poverty data is measured in international-$ at 2021 prices to account for inflation and differences in living costs between
countries. Depending on the country and year, it relates to income (measured after taxes and benefits) or to consumption, per capita. Where
data is unavailable, the closest value within 10 years is shown instead.
